title: Moon Celebration Week
venue: Royal Observatory Greenwich, National Maritime Museum and partner venues
description: Lunar talks, tours, workshops and an astrophotography evening connect space science with art and the history of Moon mapping.
accessNote: Some activities are free; tours and evening events have separate tickets. Check individual dates, age guidance and booking requirements.
notes: The programme runs 12–20 September; individual activities do not run every day.

title: Neptune at opposition · 海王星冲日
description: A telescope challenge: Neptune reaches opposition on 26 September, with the distant planet in Pisces.
accessNote: A telescope is required; Neptune is not a naked-eye target. Observatory sessions may require separate booking.
notes: 26 September evening–27 September morning is a suggested observing window around the opposition date. Visibility depends on location, horizon and weather; nearby nights are also suitable.

title: Saturn at opposition · 土星冲日
description: Saturn reaches opposition on 4 October: an inviting autumn opportunity to observe the ringed planet.
accessNote: Saturn can be seen by eye; use a telescope to resolve its rings. Local astronomy clubs may offer separate sessions.
notes: Suggested night: 4–5 October. The opportunity extends to nearby nights; local weather and horizon determine visibility.

title: Draconid meteor shower · 天龙座流星雨
description: An evening-friendly meteor watch with little moonlight. This is usually a modest shower; no exceptional outburst is predicted for 2026.
accessNote: Watch by eye from a dark, open site. No telescope is needed; access rules and weather depend on your chosen location.
notes: Viewing window: evening 8 October into 9 October. Spain's National Astronomical Observatory places maximum around 02:00 UTC on 9 October; evening viewing benefits from the higher radiant. Active 6–10 October.

title: Orionid meteor shower · 猎户座流星雨
description: Watch for fast meteors from Halley's Comet around the broad 21 October maximum.
accessNote: Choose a clear, dark site with an open sky. Moonlight may hide fainter meteors; observed numbers are not guaranteed.
notes: Two suggested nights, 20–21 and 21–22 October, around a broad maximum. The shower remains active 2 October–7 November.

title: Northern Taurids · 金牛座北流星雨
description: A quiet stargazing night with occasional slow, bright meteors around the Northern Taurids' 12 November maximum.
accessNote: Observe by eye after the crescent Moon sets. This is a low-rate shower, suited to patient observers under dark skies.
notes: Suggested viewing night: 12–13 November. The maximum is broad rather than a timed performance; the shower is active 20 October–10 December. Moonset varies by location.

title: Rencontres du Ciel et de l'Espace
venue: Cité des sciences et de l'industrie, La Villette
description: A major gathering for astronomy enthusiasts: public science talks, technical forums, workshops, exhibitions and astronomy equipment.
accessNote: Dates are confirmed by the organisers. Consult the programme and ticket information for session access and language; most programming is in French.
notes: The 15th edition runs 13–15 November 2026. This is an in-person festival, with daytime activities independent of sky conditions.

title: Leonid meteor shower · 狮子座流星雨
description: A late-night watch for fast meteors from Comet Tempel-Tuttle, with a darker sky after moonset.
accessNote: No telescope needed. Wrap up warmly and check cloud cover, local moonset and access to your chosen dark-sky site.
notes: Royal Observatory Greenwich recommends the evening of 17 November into the early hours of 18 November; the Moon sets around midnight in the UK. Times vary elsewhere. This entry does not promise a meteor storm.

title: Geminid meteor shower · 双子座流星雨
description: One of the strongest annual meteor showers, with favourable moonlight conditions in 2026 and good activity on both nights around maximum.
accessNote: Use your unaided eyes from a clear, dark location after the crescent Moon sets. Bring warm layers; the forecast rate is not an individual viewing guarantee.
notes: Viewing nights: 13–14 and 14–15 December. Spain's National Astronomical Observatory predicts a broad maximum around 14:00 UTC on 14 December (15:00 CET), so the peak instant itself falls in European daylight.

title: Ursid meteor shower · 小熊座流星雨
description: A small solstice-season shower from Comet 8P/Tuttle. Bright moonlight makes 2026 a challenging year for this quieter event.
accessNote: For patient observers: the bright Moon will wash out many meteors. Use a dark site and check weather; no telescope is needed.
notes: Two possible nights, 21–22 and 22–23 December, surround the published 22 December maximum. Active 17–26 December; the calendar dates represent a viewing window, not a precise peak instant.

title: December supermoon · 超级月亮
description: A full Moon near perigee on 24 December offers a simple seasonal skywatching and photography opportunity.
accessNote: Visible by eye when the Moon is above your local horizon and the sky is clear; a dark-sky trip is optional.
notes: Royal Observatory Greenwich identifies this date as a supermoon. Check local moonrise; this is a lunar phase date, not an eclipse or a guaranteed dramatic size change.
